newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Eletrobras signs thermoelectric deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Eletrobras signs thermoelectric deal.

text.p: Brazil's federal power holding Eletrobras has signed letters of intent with private companies for the construction of two gas-fired thermoelectric plants in Rio de Janeiro state and will release tender details for new transmission lines.

Eletrobras President Firmino Sampaio said Eletrobras will build a 450 megawatt thermoelectric plant near Macae, 188 km from Rio de Janeiro, together with the BTB consortium, which includes Australia's BHP, U.S.-firm El Paso Energy Corp and British Gas.
The plant will also include a 21.7 mile (35 km) electrical transmission line which will tie into Brazil's interconnected power system.

The other 700 megawatt thermoelectric plant will be built in partnership with Brazilian private power firms Cerj , Light, Escelsa and Cataguazes Leopoldina at a yet unknown location in Rio de Janeiro state.
Sampaio said investment in the two plants, which are expected to come on line in 1999, was estimated at 600 million reais ($560.7 million).
Eletrobras will have a 10 percent stake in the Macae plant and a 20 percent stake in the other thermoelectric plant, he said.
Eletrobras has also been authorized to publish the tenders for the construction and equipment of new transmission lines which are due to come online in December 1998.
One transmission line will link the Itaipu hydroelectric plant on the border with Paraguay to the power station at Tijuco Preto in Sao Paulo state at a cost of 500 million reais ($467.3 million).

The second transmission project, worth 738 million reais ($689.7 million), aims to connect Brazil's two transmission systems, which currently operate independently of each other in the North/Northeast and in the South/Southeast of the country.
Sampaio said the link between the two transmission systems would result in energy savings worth 600 megawatts per year.
Eletrobras is negotiating with the Inter-American Development Bank and Japan's Eximbank to obtain funding for the projects.
